justifications.c1: Large independent figures for sprinkler failure in warehouses (Primark ~£50m claim, search-confirmed; ASOS £22m stock; US $7M fire with coverage barred), but these are rare per site and none is tied to a skipped weekly pump test (Primark coverage points to a burst sprinkler supply pipe).
justifications.c2: Weekly pump test required per pump set under BS EN 12845 clause 20 and LPC TB203 (FPA page search-confirmed), echoed by Allianz and Ecclesiastical test cards and the BIF27 guide; about 52 tests per site per year, so value is demonstrable in a pilot.
justifications.c3: Documented paper test cards (Allianz, Ecclesiastical), FRS and school logbooks, and digital checklists (SafetyCulture, MaintainX) with 15–30 minute runs; Hampshire CC weighed in-house vs contractor cost but no £ or hours figure is given, and the sensor records rather than removes the pump run.
justifications.c4: BS EN 12845/TB203 mandate weekly tests and records; BAFSA (search-confirmed) says insurers impose warranties or conditions precedent, with claim refusals in Frankenmuth (7th Cir. 2023), Garvin St. (Ind. 2026) and the unnamed Magna Park 2005 case; US cases are a geography mismatch and turn on unreported impairment, not missing logs.
justifications.c5: One rotating job listing puts 'fire pump performance testing, sprinkler weekly bell testing' in an FM/duty-engineer role; no budget ownership evidenced, and the landlord vs tenant split is unresolved.
justifications.c6: LPS 1048 maintenance contractors visit at least quarterly, insurers issue the test cards, and pump OEMs sell remote fire-pump monitoring via service networks (SPP FireEye in Europe, Peerless FireConnect via Cougar Industries UK); vendor-sourced only.
justifications.c7: OEM monitors (SPP FireEye, Peerless FireConnect, Armstrong) and checklist software exist but with no prices, customer counts or complaints; the brand-neutral retrofit gap is asserted, and FM 1330 raises the bar for entrants.
justifications.c8: Parts exist (EM500-UDL €265–US$430, EM300-DI €64–120, CT310 unpriced, pressure node unpriced), so the kit runs to several hundred euros, and the file flags that FM 1330 approval or insurer/LPC acceptance may be needed before it replaces the manual log, a life-safety certification hurdle.
justifications.c9: Strong structural duty (weekly, quarterly and annual BS EN 12845/TB203 obligations plus insurer conditions at renewal), but no comparable subscription price is evidenced for FireEye, FireConnect or the checklist apps.
justifications.c10: Trade press (Retail Week, IFSEC), BAFSA fire statistics (59 fires, 17 operated), insurance-law commentary and US appellate decisions on claim denial; no UK first-hand complaint about skipped tests found.

weakest: Buildability and approval: a multi-sensor kit of several hundred euros that may need FM 1330 or insurer/LPC acceptance before it can stand in for the manual weekly log on a life-safety system.
